findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences a missing destination calendar
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when an event has no destination calendar, but the condition immediately reads `.integration`. Any booking using Google Meet without a configured destination calendar will throw before the fallback to Cal Video can run (and under strict TypeScript this is also an unsafe possibly-undefined access). Guard the value with optional chaining or an explicit existence check.

findings.title: Collective hosts' calendars are discarded when the primary host has none
findings.body: The event starts with `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor `organizerUser` has a destination calendar. The collective-host calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which is a no-op for `null`. Consequently, a collective booking where only a non-primary host has a calendar integration creates no calendar event for that host, despite that being the scenario this change is intended to support. Initialize the array from the team calendars when there is no primary destination.

findings.title: The selected destination external ID is never passed to calendar creation
findings.body: `createEvent` accepts `externalId` and records it in the returned reference, but calls the calendar implementation with only `credential.id`. `EventManager` invokes this once for every destination calendar, all using the same full `calEvent.destinationCalendar` array. Integrations that choose the first destination (for example Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV) will therefore create every host's event in the first host's calendar; Google also cannot distinguish two selected calendars using the same credential because it finds the first matching credential. Pass the target external ID through the calendar creation contract and have each implementation use it.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation only deletes the first calendar reference for each occurrence
findings.body: For each calendar reference of the original booking, the recurring cancellation loop obtains `updBooking.references.find(...)`, which always selects only the first calendar reference of each recurring occurrence. With multiple host calendar references, the additional references are never selected for deletion; the loop instead repeatedly attempts deletion of the first event, including through unrelated credentials. This leaves cancelled recurring events on secondary hosts' calendars. Match each occurrence's reference by credential ID/external calendar ID and delete it using that reference's credential.

findings.title: Rescheduling deletes multi-host calendar events with the wrong credential
findings.body: The credential lookup map is keyed only by integration type, so multiple credentials for the same provider overwrite one another. The subsequent deletion iterates all booking references but retrieves credentials by `bookingRef.type`, not `bookingRef.credentialId`. After this change a collective event can have multiple Google (or other same-provider) references, causing all deletion attempts to use one host's credential; secondary host events will fail to be deleted and remain at the old time. Build the lookup by credential ID and use each reference's credential ID.
